subsections.title: Overview
subsections.summary: What it is and why it matters.

blocks.html: A password is still the front door to almost every account you have. Most break-ins don't come from someone guessing a clever password — they come from reused passwords leaked in one breach and tried everywhere else. The fix is simple: a different, long, random password for every account, kept in a password manager, with two-factor authentication on the accounts that matter most.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.summary: The words you will run into.

items.title: Password manager
items.html: An encrypted vault that generates, stores and fills a unique password for every site, so you only remember one master password.

items.title: Passphrase
items.html: A password made of several random words. Long, easy to type, and hard to crack.

items.title: Credential stuffing
items.html: Attackers take username/password pairs leaked from one site and try them on many others. Unique passwords stop it.

items.title: Data breach
items.html: When a company loses its users’ data. Check whether your email appears in one with Have I Been Pwned.

items.title: Two-factor authentication (2FA)
items.html: A second proof of identity, like a code from an authenticator app, on top of your password.

items.title: Passkey
items.html: A newer replacement for passwords that uses a key stored on your device and can’t be phished.

subsections.title: Generate a Password
subsections.summary: A random password, made in your browser.

items.label: Bitwarden
items.desc: A solid free starting point that syncs everywhere.

items.label: KeePassXC
items.desc: Keeps your vault as a local file you control.

items.label: Proton Pass
items.desc: Includes email aliases to hide your real address.

items.label: Have I Been Pwned
items.desc: check if your email appears in a known breach.

items.label: How Secure Is My Password?
items.desc: estimate how long a password takes to crack (use a fake one).
